newsitem.title: GERMANY: German parliament tax vote postponed.
newsitem.headline: German parliament tax vote postponed.

text.p: A parliamentary vote on abolishing Germany's capital trading tax due to be held on Friday has been postponed to next week, a spokesman for the Christian Democrat (CDU/CSU) parliamentary faction said on late on Thursday.
The spokesman said there had been resistance to the move at a meeting on Thursday with Finance Minister Theo Waigel from some conservative deputies from eastern Germany.
The capital trading tax is currently levied only in western Germany, but under a constitutional court ruling would have to be imposed automatically in the east if it is not abolished.

Waigel, who argues the levy eats into the substance of company balance sheets, wants the tax scrapped. But the deputies want it imposed retroactively from January 1, 1997 to boost local government revenues.

Participants at the meeting said Waigel had offered development credits of two billion marks to municipalities in the ex-communist east to vote with him, with the possibility of a further billion marks later.

The opposition Social Democrats (SPD), who have so far blocked the tax's abolition in the Bundesrat upper house of parliament, want to link its removal to the reintroduction of a wealth tax on private fortunes.
